items.stem: Why is an existing general IT policy often insufficient for AI use?

options.text: It may not address AI-specific risks like data leakage and hallucinated output
options.rationale: Correct: AI introduces risks older policies did not cover.
IT policies are not illegal; they are just incomplete here.

options.text: AI has no risks worth a policy
A policy would ban all technology
options.rationale: A good policy enables safe use, not a blanket ban.

items.explanation: Correct: generative-AI raises new risks (data leakage to models, hallucinated output, IP) that older policies did not anticipate.
items.domain_ref: The case for an AI use policy
items.provenance: original Mastemy item drafted by an AI agent; no external question source

items.stem: Which TWO belong in the data-handling section of an AI use policy? (Select TWO.)

options.text: What categories of data may and may not be entered into AI tools
options.rationale: Correct: data classification rules are essential.

options.text: How confidential and personal data must be handled
options.rationale: Correct: confidentiality and PII handling belong here.
Formatting is not a data-handling rule.

items.explanation: Correct: rules on what data may be shared and confidentiality/PII handling are core data-handling provisions.

items.stem: Why do AI use policies often define risk tiers instead of one blanket rule?

options.text: Different uses carry different risk and need proportionate controls
options.rationale: Correct: tiering matches controls to risk.

options.text: Tiers make the policy longer for its own sake
options.rationale: Length is not the purpose; proportionate control is.

options.text: All AI use is identically risky
Tiers remove the need for any human oversight
options.rationale: Higher tiers usually add oversight, not remove it.

items.explanation: Correct: different uses carry different risk, so tiers match oversight and approvals to the risk level.
